image-converter.formula:
PNG -> JPEG: pixels are re-encoded with lossy compression at the chosen quality.
Transparent pixel -> background color: JPEG has no alpha channel, so each
semi-transparent pixel is blended: out = fg x alpha + bg x (1 - alpha).
Example: 50% red (255,0,0) over white (255,255,255):
out = 255 x 0.5 + 255 x 0.5 = 255, 0 x 0.5 + 255 x 0.5 = 127.5 -> rgb(255, 128, 128).
howTo: Choose an image file up to 50 MB - JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP or SVG.

keyFacts: JPEG uses lossy compression and cannot store transparency - transparent areas are filled with your chosen background color.
PNG uses lossless compression and keeps transparency, but files are larger.
WebP supports both transparency and lossy compression - usually the smallest option.
SVG and GIF inputs are rasterised: the current frame is drawn as pixels, animation is not preserved.
EXIF metadata (camera settings, GPS) is not copied to the converted file.
Converting from a lossy format to PNG never restores detail - it only changes the container.

image-converter.workedExample:
Convert a 200 x 100 transparent PNG logo to JPEG with a white background.
1. The canvas is filled white first: every pixel starts as rgb(255, 255, 255).
2. The logo is drawn on top. A 50% transparent red pixel blends:
   out = fg x alpha + bg x (1 - alpha)
   = (255 x 0.5 + 255 x 0.5, 0 x 0.5 + 255 x 0.5, 0 x 0.5 + 255 x 0.5)
   = rgb(255, 128, 128) - soft pink where the edge fades.
3. Fully transparent areas stay pure white: rgb(255, 255, 255).
4. The result is encoded as JPEG at your quality and downloaded as logo-converted.jpg.
